svg.title: Environment to valid solutions and solutions polytope
svg.desc: Full figure inventory: left Environment section contains title, robot arm, table with package, orange right arrow, and Task Reward r label with a red dashed reward vector toward the valid-solutions point. Central section contains a tilted gray all-solutions plane with dotted border, black coordinate axes, orange half-space labels, a blue valid-solutions polygon with white label and a blue point. Gray dashed correspondence lines connect central solutions to the right. Right section contains a large light-blue solutions polytope with dark border, three blue points and dashed arrows labeled w1,w2 to a policy rectangle with labels pi1, pi2, pi*. Symmetry basis: overall layout is left-to-right process flow, central construction is oblique projection, right section uses three horizontally equipartitioned policy rays.

g.desc: Orange rightward process arrow from environment to solution-space construction.

Central section origin is the blue point inside the valid-solutions polygon. Upward black axis, lower-left black axis, and lower-right black axis radiate from/near the solution point and plane intersection. The gray tilted plane indicates all solutions and the blue polygon indicates valid solutions inside a labeled half-space.
Dashed gray guide lines preserve oblique projection relationship from central solution region to right solutions polytope.

Right section origin relation: the large polygon is reached from the central valid-solution point by gray dashed correspondence lines. Three internal blue points are horizontally aligned to policy outputs pi1, pi2, and pi* with dashed blue arrows.

Original Figure Object: robot arm. Constructed Element ID: draft_robot. SAM Asset ID: asset_sam_region_000008. The crop covers the robot only and preserves the environment title and task reward text outside the crop.

Original Figure Object: table with package. Constructed Element ID: draft_table_box. SAM Asset ID: asset_sam_region_000009. The crop is used as a unified block to avoid duplicating the overlapping cube-only crop.
